name: Opentrons Labworks, Inc.
origin_detail: Founded 2014 in Brooklyn by Will Canine, Chiu Chau and Nicholas Wagner, who met through the DIYbio listserv / Genspace community lab; HAXLR8TR (Shenzhen) hardware accelerator, Kickstarter late 2014 ($126k from 237 backers), Y Combinator W16. HQ now Long Island City, NY.
flagship_projects: Opentrons App + Python Protocol API (Apache-2.0 monorepo)
openness_notes: OT-One (2015, $2,000) shipped with hardware files on GitHub (Opentrons/otone_hardware: laser-cut DXF, STL, BOM spreadsheets) under Apache-2.0; Wikipedia notes editable source CAD was not released. From the OT-2 (2018) onward hardware is proprietary (only coarse enclosure CAD), while the robot software, app, robot-server, Python Protocol API and labware definitions remain Apache-2.0 on GitHub (opentrons monorepo, ~540 stars / ~220 forks). The 2024 EULA says only 'certain components' are Apache-2.0. The 2026 Series E release markets 'open, API-driven' robots but never claims open-source hardware. Net: open software + closed hardware = level 2 on the hardware scale.

license_history.license: Apache-2.0 (OT-One hardware files: DXF/STL/BOM; plus software)
license_history.note: Repository describes 'independent construction of the opensource OT.One lab automation platform'
Only coarse enclosure CAD released for OT-2; Wikipedia statement carries a citation-needed tag
Contributions accepted under Apache-2.0 per CONTRIBUTING.md

relicensing_events.from: Open hardware files (OT-One, Apache-2.0) + open software
relicensing_events.outcome_note: Not a licence change on existing files but a closing of new product designs; no community fork of the robot emerged, though OT-One models live on in hobby projects (e.g. pipettin-bot on GitLab). The OT-2 became Opentrons' volume product.

risk_events: 2018: OT-2 launched as closed hardware; open-hardware status lost (software stayed Apache-2.0)
Sep 2021: $200M Series C led by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 at ~$1.8B (Bloomberg), up from ~$90M in 2020, on COVID-testing growth
Dec 31 2022: Pandemic Response Lab (subsidiary ReOpen Diagnostics, NYC COVID testing) wound down, all ~185 jobs eliminated (Bloomberg)
2022-2025: headcount drifted from ~276 to ~223 (Revelio Labs); anonymous Glassdoor reviews describe repeated layoffs incl. the PRL division (unverified)
Jul 2025 (announced 30 Jan 2026): CEO changed from co-founder Jon Brennan-Badal to James Atwood (ex-PerkinElmer/MOBILion, GM of robotics unit since Apr 2023)
20 Nov 2025: Series D/D-1 (~$20M, BroadOak, SOSV) at ~$162M post-money per Forge, roughly 91% below the 2021 valuation (my arithmetic)
29 Oct 2026: $40M Series E led by Avego with BroadOak, SoftBank and Khosla, repositioned as 'AI-native' lab automation; Forge estimates ~$170M post-money
robustness: Single-vendor company with no foundation, but the whole control stack (app, robot server, Python API, labware schema) is Apache-2.0 on GitHub, so protocols and integrations could outlive the firm. Current hardware designs are proprietary, so the community could not build or repair OT-2/Flex robots independently. Large installed base (>11,000 robots in >80 countries, 14 of top-15 biopharmas, every top-20 US research university per the 2026 release) and survival through a ~91% valuation reset suggest a durable niche.
physical_science_relevance: Built for life-science liquid handling, but the OT-2 is one of the most common low-cost liquid handlers in academic materials/chemistry automation: e.g. precursor preparation for high-throughput sonochemical synthesis (RSC Digital Discovery 2023), CdSe nanocrystal synthesis paired with the Jubilee platform (MRS 2024), and Turkevich gold-nanoparticle teaching protocols (LAPSE 2026). Limited to pipettable liquids (no powders/solids). The requesting lab (BYU VCL) itself runs an OT-2 in its color-mixing SDL.
openness_effect_assessment: Openness was the founding go-to-market: a $2,000 open-hardware OT-One crowdfunded from the DIYbio/academic community built the brand ('the PC of biotech labs', TechCrunch 2016) and a user-written protocol ecosystem. Opentrons then closed the hardware with the OT-2 (2018) while keeping the software open, which preserved scriptability and SDL integration without handing designs to cloners; no fork of the robot emerged. The 2021 peak ($1.8B) and the 2022-2025 collapse (~$162M) were driven by COVID testing and its end, not by the openness choice.
key_takeaway: Opentrons is the canonical open-hardware lab-automation test case, and its arc is 'open to enter, close the hardware to scale': the open OT-One won early users cheaply, but revenue came from a closed-hardware OT-2/Flex whose open Apache-2.0 API is the remaining open asset and the reason it dominates academic self-driving-lab builds. Its valuation fell about 91% from the 2021 SoftBank round to the 2025 Series D, a COVID boom-and-bust rather than a verdict on openness. In 2026 it repositioned as 'open, AI-native' infrastructure connecting AI to the wet lab, marketing 'open' as API access rather than open designs.
notes: funding_total_usd = Forge Global sum of preferred-stock issuances from Certificates of Incorporation (through the Oct 2026 Series E). CB Insights lists $260.2M total equity funding; announced round sizes (e.g. $200M Series C) exceed Forge's share-issuance totals (~$117M for Series C), possibly because part of the round was secondary. Treat as a range of roughly $206M-$300M.
latest_value_usd is Forge's estimated Series E post-money from charter filings, not a company-disclosed valuation; the company did not disclose a valuation.
Series D amount differs by source ($15.6M+$4.5M per Forge; $20.1M per Multiples.vc/Form D, from a $56.6M offering).
employees_latest is a Revelio Labs estimate (June 2026); Wikipedia lists 328 (2023); other trackers give 194-214 for 2026.
